sources.citation: Swanton, John R. 1940. Linguistic Material from the Tribes of Southern Texas and Northeastern Mexico. Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 127. Washington: GPO. (Glottolog ref 62513; listed by Glottolog as an overview;minimal; language code Payaya, Aranama, San Francisco Solano)

sources.note: Nothing. Payaya appears three times: p. 5 'We also have a single word from the tongue of the Payaya who lived on or near the Rio San Antonio'; p. 55 (Additional Coahuilteco words from the mission records) 'yana wana (yana guana), the San Antonio River. In the language of the Payaya tribe which lived upon it.'; p. 135 in the conjectural list of Coahuiltecan bands. No accent marks, no phonology, no wordlist (the earlier scan note's '25-item wordlist' is wrong: it is one word).
